lines.text: Wall Street's bet on an October Fed rate hike collapsed this week.

lines.text: After a hot inflation report on October 14, the odds jumped from 22% to as high as 50%, per CME FedWatch.
lines.say: After a hot inflation report on October fourteenth, the odds jumped from twenty-two to as high as fifty percent, per C M E FedWatch.

lines.text: Then on October 16, Fed Chair Kevin Warsh said: "I don't prejudge meetings."

lines.text: With no hint either way, the odds fell to about 15%, CNBC reported.
lines.say: With no hint either way, the odds fell to about fifteen percent, CNBC reported.

lines.text: The Fed already raised rates on September 16, to 3.75% to 4%.
lines.say: The Fed already raised rates on September sixteenth, to three point seven five to four percent.

lines.text: Fed officials went quiet on October 17, ahead of the October 28 decision.

lines.text: Why care? The Fed's rate flows into credit card APRs, savings yields and home equity lines.

post.title: Wall Street's bet on an October Fed hike collapsed this week
post.ig:
Wall Street's bet on an October Fed rate hike collapsed this week.
After the hot Sept CPI report on Oct 14, CME FedWatch odds of an October hike jumped from 22% to as high as 50%.
On Oct 16, Fed Chair Kevin Warsh said "I don't prejudge meetings," and the odds fell to about 15% (CNBC).
The Fed raised rates to 3.75%-4% on Sept 16. Its quiet period began Oct 17; the decision is Oct 28.
Sources: Federal Reserve, CME FedWatch, CNBC, Reuters, Benzinga.
News and education, not financial advice.
